name: hra-reference-organs
title: HRA Reference Organs — Uberon-Keyed Organ Set
question:
Does the HRA CCF API's reference-organs endpoint load into a Step-driven
composite, giving an Uberon-keyed organ set (with per-sex GLB assets)?

study_card.goal: Fetch HRA reference organs via HRAReferenceOrgansStep and confirm the composite loads a non-empty, Uberon-annotated organ list.
study_card.expected_result: The full HRA reference-organ set (~77 organs, some sex-split) loads with a parsed organ slug, Uberon (or FMA) CURIE, sex, and GLB asset URL per entry.
study_card.main_expert_question: Is the reference-organ set stable enough (schema + coverage) to key downstream biomodel annotation off of?

biological_summary:
The HRA reference-organ set is the atlas's per-sex, whole-organ 3D
scaffold: each entry is a single named organ (or organ pair, e.g. kidney
left/right) rendered as its own GLB asset, sex-split where anatomy
differs (breast, reproductive organs) and unsplit where it doesn't (most
visceral organs). This set is the anchor everything else in
`hra-integration` keys off of: `glucose-biomodel-do`'s synonym matching
scans these organ slugs, and `hra-3d`'s crosswalk propagates coverage
from each organ's Uberon CURIE down to every anatomical-structure node
cut from its GLB.

report.title: HRA Reference Organs — 81 organs loaded, 69/81 (85.2%) Uberon-keyed, 45 female / 36 male
report.objective:
Does the HRA CCF API's reference-organs endpoint load into a
Step-driven composite, giving an Uberon-keyed organ set (with per-sex
GLB assets)?
report.conclusion:
A live run against `https://apps.humanatlas.io/api/v1/reference-organs`
returned 81 reference-organ entries spanning 58 distinct organ slugs
(bilateral/sex-specific organs like kidney or ovary contribute more
than one entry). 69/81 (85.2%) carry a UBERON-prefixed CURIE; the
remaining 12 (14.8%) parse to a non-Uberon (FMA) identifier. The set
splits 45 female-specific / 36 male-specific entries, reflecting
per-sex organ GLBs (breast, reproductive organs) plus duplicated
unisex organs modeled once per sex.
report.caveat:
"Uberon-keyed" here means the parsed CURIE prefix is literally
`UBERON:`; the 14.8% FMA-prefixed entries are not un-annotated, just on
a different ontology, so downstream Uberon-keyed matching
(`glucose-biomodel-do`'s organ index, `hra-3d`'s crosswalk) silently
drops them rather than flagging a translation gap.

readouts: fraction of organs with a UBERON-prefixed uberon CURIE (vs FMA)
